transcript:
[doctor] Hello, good to see you today. How have you been feeling?

[patient] Hi, Doctor. I've been really tired and just not myself lately.

[doctor] I'm sorry to hear that. Can you describe what’s been going on?

[patient] Sure, I’ve been really hungry and thirsty all the time, and I’ve been getting up a lot at night to use the bathroom. I also feel exhausted all the time. It’s been going on for about four months now.

[doctor] That sounds quite challenging. You mentioned feeling fatigued and having to take frequent breaks at work. Has this affected your daily activities?

[patient] Yes, definitely. I can't focus at work, and I’ve stopped exercising because I just don’t have the energy.

[doctor] I understand. Let’s review some systems. Have you noticed any changes in your vision or any eye problems?

[patient] I have mild cataracts, but I haven't noticed any new vision changes.

[doctor] Okay, and how about your breathing? Any shortness of breath or wheezing?

[patient] Yes, I do get short of breath and sometimes I wheeze.

[doctor] Alright, any chest pain or palpitations?

[patient] No chest pain or palpitations.

[doctor] What about any abdominal pain or issues with your liver?

[patient] I haven’t had any abdominal pain, but I do know I have a fatty liver.

[doctor] Got it. And how about your urinary habits? Any blood in your urine or just the frequent nighttime trips?

[patient] Just the frequent nighttime trips, no blood.

[doctor] Any joint pain or issues with your muscles?

[patient] No, no joint pain.

[doctor] And you mentioned being very hungry and thirsty. Any issues with your mood, like anxiety or depression?

[patient] No, I haven’t had any anxiety or depression.

[doctor] Thanks for that. Let’s talk about your past medical history. You have Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD), correct?

[patient] Yes, that's right.

[doctor] How about your family history? Any significant illnesses?

[patient] My father had hypertension and my mother had rheumatoid arthritis.

[doctor] Okay, and what about your social history? Do you smoke or drink?

[patient] I quit smoking five years ago after smoking a pack daily for 20 years. I drink beer socially, about 3-4 drinks a week.

[doctor] Good to know you quit smoking. What about recreational activities? Do you have any hobbies?

[patient] I enjoy fishing, but I haven’t been able to go lately because I feel too tired.

[doctor] Alright. Let’s go over your current medications. You're using an Albuterol inhaler as needed and taking Atorvastatin 20 mg daily, correct?

[patient] Yes, that’s right.

[doctor] Any allergies?

[patient] Yes, I’m allergic to shellfish.

[doctor] Thank you for sharing all this information. Let’s take a look at your vital signs. Your blood pressure today is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 82 bpm, and your BMI is 35.5 kg/m².

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] I also see you’re short of breath after minimal exertion and your respiratory exam shows decreased breath sounds bilaterally with wheezing. Your cardiovascular exam shows a regular heartbeat with no murmurs, and your peripheral pulses are palpable with no edema.

[patient] That sounds about right.

[doctor] Your abdominal exam shows mild hepatomegaly. There's also mild edema and varicosities in your extremities.

[patient] I see.

[doctor] I’ve ordered some blood work, including Hemoglobin A1c, Fasting Plasma Glucose, and Kidney Function Tests. We also need to get an abdominal ultrasound to check on your liver.

[patient] Alright, that sounds good.

[doctor] Given your symptoms and history, I’m diagnosing you with hyperglycemia due to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, COPD, NAFLD, and hypertension.

[patient] What should I do now?

[doctor] We need to start you on some new medications. I’m prescribing Liraglutide 1.2 mg injection, to be taken subcutaneously once daily, and Sitagliptin 100 mg, to be taken orally once daily.

[patient] Okay, I can do that.

[doctor] Along with the medications, we need to focus on some lifestyle changes. I recommend you start a weight loss program and follow a balanced diet with more fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Also, increase your physical activities, starting with low-impact exercises. Try to replace sugary drinks with water.

[patient] I’ll try my best.

[doctor] Great. We’ll schedule a follow-up appointment in 6 weeks to assess how the medications are working and to see how you're doing with the lifestyle changes.

[patient] Alright, that sounds good.

[doctor] During the follow-up, we can also discuss any concerns you might have about medication costs and explore affordable alternatives.

[patient] That would be helpful.

[doctor] Don’t forget to keep up with your regular pulmonary care for your COPD and to manage your high blood pressure. Diet and exercise will help with both hypertension and diabetes.

[patient] I understand.

[doctor] Do you have any questions or concerns right now?

[patient] No, I think you've covered everything.

[doctor] Excellent. Let’s get started on these plans, and we’ll see you back in 6 weeks. Take care.

[patient] Thank you, Doctor. See you in 6 weeks.
